clue.text: Tumble dryer's a "gift" found at entrance for scrap-heap

indicators.note: being at the entrance means standing first, so this piece goes before the rest

parts.note: a gift or natural talent for something is a knack

indicators.note: to tumble is to fall and roll over, so the letters are tossed into a new order

parts.note: the letters of these words, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Someone is sarcastically calling a broken tumble dryer a gift, left by the front door for the tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tumble dryer' reads as one appliance, but 'Tumble' is the instruction and 'dryer's a' the letters. A knacker's yard is where worn-out horses were slaughtered.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively, the knacker's yard is where worn-out things end up, an idiom for being fit only for disposal.

clue.text: Black tea — or tea no milk — made last of all in public bars?

definitions.note: a phrase describing where the answer happens rather than a noun

indicators.note: the final letter of every word is wanted, so only each word's end is kept

parts.note: end of the word
end of the word
end of the word
ends of both words
end of the word
end of the word

explanation.surface: A fussy drinker's order of black tea, no milk, made at closing time in the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: The drinks order is pure fodder: take the last letter of each word from 'Black' to 'made'. The question mark flags the loose, descriptive definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Karaoke singing is a familiar evening entertainment staged in pubs, so the answer is something found in public bars.

clue.text: A small number supporting Italy — absurd

indicators.note: in a down entry, what supports something sits beneath it, so this piece follows

parts.note: taken as written
S is the standard abbreviation for small
I is the international vehicle code for Italy
any number will do; this one fits

explanation.surface: A complaint that backing Italy with only a handful of people is ridiculous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small number' looks like one phrase, but small is just S and the number is nine, placed under Italy in the column.
explanation.definitionFit: Asinine literally means like an ass, and is a common synonym for stupid or ridiculous.

clue.text: Heather's family discussed by Spooner somewhere in Norfolk

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts of two words trade places

parts.note: ling is another name for heather; it takes the opening sound of the other word
kin means family; it takes the opening sound of the first word

explanation.surface: A woman called Heather has her relatives talked over by a man named Spooner, who lives in Norfolk.
explanation.walkthrough: Heather is not a person's name but the plant, also called ling. Swap the initial sounds of 'ling's kin' to reach the town.
explanation.definitionFit: King's Lynn is a port and market town in the English county of Norfolk, so it is one place there.

clue.text: Part of staircase RE teacher climbs

indicators.note: climbing in a down entry means travelling upward, so this piece runs bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
pupils address a male teacher as sir

explanation.surface: The religious education teacher walks up the school stairs.
explanation.walkthrough: RE (religious education) is lifted straight, then the whole thing is read upward with the teacher. 'Part of staircase' sits in the scene too, which is the disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: On a staircase, the riser is the vertical board between one tread and the next, a component of every step.

clue.text: Caddie's estimate of area covered by electronic golf cart going uphill

indicators.note: something covered by others is wrapped by them, so it sits within
in a down entry going uphill means reading from the bottom up

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail
golf is G in the NATO phonetic alphabet
A is the abbreviation for area
a dray is a low cart for heavy loads

explanation.surface: A caddie estimates a distance while riding an electric buggy up a slope on the course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Electronic golf cart' reads as one vehicle, but it splits into E, G and DRAY, with the area tucked between, all then read upward. A caddie carries clubs and advises a golfer.
explanation.definitionFit: A caddie gauges the distance in yards to the flag, and that measured length is the yardage.

clue.text: Pawn souvenir cases along with a copy

indicators.note: along with means added on beside, so one piece simply follows another
to case something is to enclose it, as a box encloses its contents

parts.note: a relic is a keepsake from the past
P is the chess notation for pawn
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone pawns a set of souvenir display cases, together with a fake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pawn' reads as a verb about hocking goods, but it is the chess piece; 'cases' looks like a noun but is the verb to enclose.
explanation.definitionFit: A replica is an exact reproduction of an original object, so it is a synonym for a copy.

clue.text: One can't pinch faulty furniture van

indicators.note: something faulty is broken or out of order, so the letters need rearranging

parts.note: the letters of these words, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A thief laments that a broken-down removal lorry is impossible to steal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Faulty furniture van' reads as one phrase, but 'faulty' works on the three words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a pantechnicon is an old-fashioned name for a large removal lorry used to move household furniture.

clue.text: Hearing a command: charge

indicators.note: a hearing is what the ear receives, so the words are judged by their sound

parts.note: a reign is a period of command or rule

explanation.surface: At a court hearing, an order is given to bring a charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearing' looks like the courtroom session, which suits the definition, but it signals sound. A reign, a spell of rule, stands for a command here.
explanation.definitionFit: To arraign is to formally call an accused person before a court to answer an indictment.

clue.text: Piece journalist filed

parts.note: a scrap is a small piece of something
ED is short for editor, the stock crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter has submitted their article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece' and 'filed' both suggest newspaper copy, but 'filed' means rubbed with a file.
explanation.definitionFit: Working metal with a file abrades its surface, so a filed edge has been scraped smooth.

clue.text: Perhaps Dirk's tired in state of open hostility

definitions.note: a phrase for a state; the answer is used in the idiom 'at daggers drawn'

parts.note: dirks are Scottish daggers, one example of the type, so 'perhaps' signals the example
a drawn face looks tired and strained

explanation.surface: A man called Dirk is weary from being in constant conflict.
explanation.walkthrough: Dirk looks like a man's name (the actor Dirk Bogarde, say), but a dirk is a dagger, and the apostrophe is a red herring for the plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at daggers drawn is an idiom for open enmity, as if two rivals had pulled their blades.

clue.text: Queen has subjects touring equatorial regions

indicators.note: a touring party goes around a place, so one piece goes around another

parts.note: topics are subjects for discussion
R is short for regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: The monarch takes her subjects on a royal tour of Commonwealth countries near the equator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Subjects' suggests royal subjects but means topics of discussion, which go around the queen's letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The tropics are the hot zones either side of the equator, bounded by Cancer and Capricorn.

clue.text: Understanding a county town

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the county town of Berkshire, west of London

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like praise for a sympathetic town; it is two meanings. A county town is the administrative centre of an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: Your reading of something is your interpretation of it, and the Berkshire town shares the same spelling.

clue.text: Material salesman used to plug Coca-Cola not OK

indicators.note: a plug fills a gap, so one piece is stuffed into another
not means without, so these letters must be taken away

parts.note: Coke is the brand's short name
taken as written
a rep is a sales representative

explanation.surface: A fabric salesman is enlisted to promote a cola that has fallen out of favour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plug' suggests advertising, but here it means filling a hole. Strip OK from the cola's short name, then put the salesman in the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: Crepe is a thin crinkled fabric, a type of material used for dresses and scarves.

clue.text: Finally play Spice Girls' Wannabe as on broadcast — keep stopping song

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so each word gives its closing letter

parts.note: the final letter of each of the three words

indicators.note: a stopper sits inside a neck, so one piece is lodged inside the other
to broadcast is to scatter widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

parts.note: the letters of these words
to keep something is to have it

explanation.surface: A radio presenter keeps playing the Spice Girls' hit Wannabe, interrupting another song.
explanation.walkthrough: The italic Wannabe looks like the song title in play, but it is fodder; the answer is a 1920s novelty song. 'Keep' supplies a verb that sits inside the shuffled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Yes! We Have No Bananas is a 1923 American novelty hit, a famous popular song still widely known.

clue.text: Made legal claim assuming pay out is deferred

indicators.note: to assume is to take on or take in, so one piece takes another inside

parts.note: to sue is to make a legal claim against someone
to spend is to pay out money

explanation.surface: A lawsuit was filed on the assumption that a payout would be postponed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Assuming' reads as 'supposing', but here it means taking something in.
explanation.definitionFit: A suspended sentence or payment has been put off until later, so suspended is a synonym for postponed.

clue.text: See 14
Finding ghetto-blaster in two different Spars

parts.note: the two pieces are both spars, in different senses
a boom is a spar along the foot of a sail
to spar is to box, as in practice fighting

explanation.surface: Someone discovers a portable stereo in two branches of the Spar convenience store chain.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital S suggests Spar, a chain of small grocery shops in Britain; the word is two meanings at once, a ship's pole and to box.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghetto-blaster is a large portable stereo with loudspeakers; boombox is the more common American name.

clue.text: Faster shot meeting upright

parts.note: a nip is a small shot of spirits
a pier is an upright pillar supporting a bridge or arch

explanation.surface: A sprinter fires off a quicker shot and clips the post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' and 'upright' sound like sport, a ball striking a goalpost; they are a drink and a pillar.
explanation.definitionFit: Nippy is informal British for quick and agile, so the comparative nippier means more speedy.

clue.text: Tricks Republican exploits

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for Republican
to exploit something is to use it

explanation.surface: A politician's deceptions are exploits, daring feats of trickery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exploits' looks like a noun meaning adventures but works as the verb for making use of.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruses are cunning stratagems meant to deceive, a direct synonym for tricks.

clue.text: Person I groomed enlists

indicators.note: grooming tidies and rearranges, so the letters are set in a fresh order

parts.note: the letters of these words

explanation.surface: Someone I have coached and prepared signs up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Person I groomed' reads as a single noun phrase; 'groomed' acts on the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: To rope someone in is an idiom for persuading them to join or help, much like recruiting.

clue.text: Makes great effort in Cornish resort when crossing river

indicators.note: to cross something is to span it, so the outer piece reaches around the inner

parts.note: St Ives is a seaside town in Cornwall
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker in a Cornish seaside town works hard to get across a river.
explanation.walkthrough: Cornwall is the county at the south-west tip of England; its resort wraps around the river.
explanation.definitionFit: To strive is to try very hard or struggle toward a goal, matching an earnest effort.

clue.text: Case of censor having pages in dictionary cut

indicators.note: a case is an outer shell, so only the outside letters are kept

parts.note: first and last letters

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: OED is the Oxford English Dictionary
pp is the abbreviation for pages

explanation.surface: A censor takes a case against a dictionary for its pages being trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case of censor' sounds like a legal matter but only wants the outside of the word. 'Cut' reads as part of the story yet is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Cropped describes something trimmed short, such as hair or a photograph, so it is a synonym for cut.

clue.text: Nobleman's fists

definitions.note: read as 'noblemen', plural nouns, the possessive apostrophe is ignored
definitions.meaning: first meaning: peers of the highest rank below a prince

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as an aristocrat's hands; it is two separate meanings, the second old slang from boxing.
explanation.definitionFit: Dukes are the top rank of the British peerage, and in slang the same word is used for clenched hands ready to fight.

clue.text: Sulks after banks must withdraw gold sovereign

indicators.note: once the banks withdraw, the edges are gone, so the outer letters are removed

parts.note: fits of bad mood; to be in a temper is close to sulking
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A financier sulks once the banks are forced to pull out of the gold market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banks' and 'withdraw gold' paint a financial picture, but 'banks' are the edges of a word, which is trimmed at both ends before the heraldic gold is added.
explanation.definitionFit: An emperor is the supreme ruler of an empire, so he is a sovereign in the sense of a monarch.

clue.text: Faldo pockets one pound in return for old golf club

indicators.note: to pocket something is to put it away inside, so one piece holds another

parts.note: Nick Faldo is the English golfer, six-time major champion
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so these letters run backwards

parts.note: lb is the abbreviation for a pound in weight

explanation.surface: Golfer Nick Faldo accepts a single pound in exchange for an antique club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound' looks like money in the deal, but it is the unit of weight. The golfing scene matches the answer, a nice touch.
explanation.definitionFit: A niblick was an old name for a lofted iron golf club, roughly equivalent to a modern nine-iron.

clue.text: Pop video was lacking energy — reject

indicators.note: to pop is to burst, so the letters fly apart and land in a new order
lacking means going without, so these letters are left out

parts.note: the letters of these words
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A pop music video was flat and lifeless, so it was turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop video' reads as a music clip; 'Pop' is the instruction, after 'video was' loses its energy.
explanation.definitionFit: To disavow is to deny responsibility for or repudiate something, a formal synonym for rejecting it.

clue.text: Obama, Clinton say Biden initially ignored Trump's biggest feature — breaking report

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it

parts.note: to express a fact is to state or report it

indicators.note: ignoring the start means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
the capital T is the tallest letter in the name

explanation.surface: Two former presidents notice that Biden overlooked Trump's most prominent trait in a news report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Biggest feature' tempts a guess about Trump himself, but it is simply his name's capital letter. 'Say' marks the two presidents as examples.
explanation.definitionFit: Obama and Clinton are both former holders of the US presidency, examples of the men who once led the country.
